:::{#def-affine-subspace}
#### Affine subspace

An **affine subspace** of $\reals^p$ is a set of the form

$$
\cb{\vecf{x}_0 + \vecf{s} : \vecf{s} \in \mathcal{S}}
$$

for some vector $\vecf{x}_0 \in \reals^p$ and some subspace $\mathcal{S}$ of $\reals^p$ (@def-subspace):
the [image](sets-functions.qmd#def-image) of $\mathcal{S}$
under the translation by $\vecf{x}_0$ (@def-translation).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-affine-subspace}
#### A line that misses the origin is an affine subspace

The line $\mathcal{T} = \cb{(x, 1) : x \in \reals}$ of @exm-not-subspace is not a subspace,
but it is an affine subspace,
with $\vecf{x}_0 = (0, 1)$ and $\mathcal{S} = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 0)}$ (@def-span):

$$
\ba
(0, 1) + c\,(1, 0)
&= (0 + c,\; 1 + 0)
&& \text{(@def-scalar-mult, @def-vector-addition)}
\\
&= (c, 1),
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

and as $c$ ranges over $\reals$, $(c, 1)$ ranges over all of $\mathcal{T}$.
Every subspace $\mathcal{S}$ is also an affine subspace, with $\vecf{x}_0 = \vzero$.

:::
